title: Ticket history disappears after logical PostgreSQL data loss
customer_impact: The ticket API remains reachable and returns HTTP 200, but all ticket history is missing from the customer-visible dataset.
scope: Logical loss is isolated to tickets/ticket_events. PostgreSQL remains reachable, API readiness stays healthy, the schema contract remains valid, and the 100,000-row customer_activity workload is still present.

timeline.event: Customer data-integrity validation detected an empty ticket list while service readiness remained healthy.
L2 acknowledged the incident and confirmed PostgreSQL reachability plus the intact database schema.
Database inventory confirmed tickets=0 while customer_activity remained at its 100,000-row baseline, proving localized logical data loss.
The pre-incident custom-format backup checksum and catalog were verified; a clean validation restore had already matched the baseline ticket count, fingerprint, schema contract, and activity count.
Approved simulated database recovery stopped the API, recreated the primary database, and restored from the previously validated backup.
Post-restore validation confirmed schema contract, ticket count/fingerprint, activity count, API readiness, ticket read path, and transactional write capability.

evidence: pre-loss backup was created with pg_dump custom format and its SHA-256 checksum was retained
pg_restore catalog contained ticket and customer_activity table data
backup was restored successfully into a separate clean validation database before destructive testing
validation restore matched baseline ticket count, ticket fingerprint, customer_activity count, and schema contract
during loss PostgreSQL and /health/ready remained healthy
during loss /api/tickets returned HTTP 200 with zero ticket rows
customer_activity remained at 100,000 rows while tickets dropped to zero
primary database was rebuilt from the previously validated backup rather than from an untested artifact
post-restore ticket count and deterministic fingerprint matched baseline
post-restore customer_activity count matched baseline and the ticket API returned the restored dataset
resolution: L2 identified localized logical data loss rather than a PostgreSQL outage. Recovery used a pre-incident custom-format backup that had already passed an independent clean-restore validation. The primary database was recreated and restored, then schema, business-data fingerprints, customer API behavior, and transactional capability were re-verified before resolution.
